text: That afternoon: Holmes says that he and Watson must spend the night in her room
why: Holmes's line at ¶178 is stated in the story, and Holmes said at ¶82 that they would arrive early in the afternoon.

text: What will happen in the middle room to-night?
why: A plain question the story gives every reason to raise: Helen sleeps in the middle room, where her sister died after hearing the whistle.

text: What will happen in the middle room to-night? — the whistle comes, and something passes through the ventilator to the bed
id: q.tonight=the whistle comes, and something passes through the ventilator to the bed
why: A possibility the text prompts: the ventilator opens into another room, the bell-rope is a dummy hung just above it, and the whistle has been heard. The label's specific course of events goes beyond the text, but the possibility itself is open to a reader.

text: What will happen in the middle room to-night? — nothing: Dr. Roylott lies low now that Holmes is on to him
id: q.tonight=nothing: Dr. Roylott lies low now that Holmes is on to him
why: A reasonable possibility to consider: Holmes has shown himself to Roylott and Roylott has been warned off, and the story has not yet ruled out that he will keep quiet.

text: What will happen in the middle room to-night? — Dr. Roylott tries to get at her by open violence
